title: Fixing a Choice Commutes with Phase Hosting
statement: Let $I$ be an index type, let $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ be a state type for each $i\in I$, and let $M_i$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with state set $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and a common tape count and symbol alphabet. Choose an initial state in the dependent sum of these state types and a reduction map that assigns to each phase state either no new state or a phase state in that sum. For either choice bit $b$, fixing choice $b$ in the phase-hosted machine gives the same deterministic machine as phase-hosting the machines obtained by fixing choice $b$ in each $M_i$.
hypotheses_covered: A state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ for each $i\in I$
A family of nondeterministic machines $M_i$ with common tape count and symbol alphabet
A reduction map from each phase state to an optional dependent-sum state
